title: A pre-registered test on a second interictal clip from 56 HUP patients repeated the human iEEG timescale gradient along cortical T1w/T2w; clip state changed mean timescale but not the gradient
abstract: Question: is the human iEEG timescale gradient along cortical T1w/T2w (sci:84905fb5, post hoc model) present in new data under a pre-registered test? Data: OpenNeuro ds004100 v1.1.3 (HUP iEEG, CC0), interictal run-02, a second 300-s clip that no campaign study had analysed; 2,454 bipolar cortical channels in 56 patients outside seizure-onset and resection zones. Method: plan hashed before analysis; code of the earlier study unchanged; FOOOF knee timescale tau; OLS of log10 tau on z(T1w/T2w) with patient fixed effects, surface distance and bipolar spacing, without the delta-power covariate; 2,000 patient-bootstrap samples and 1,000 sphere rotations (spin test). Rule: CI below 0 and p_spin < 0.05. Results: the primary test passed. The slope was -0.073 log10 tau per SD (95% CI -0.095 to -0.051; p_spin 0.022), 15% shorter tau per SD, almost the same as run-01 (-0.072, reproduced exactly). The per-patient correlation was negative in 44 of 55 patients (sign p 9e-6). Channel tau had rho 0.85 between the two clips inside patients. A change in relative delta power between clips moved the mean tau of a patient (rho 0.73) but not the T1w/T2w slope (rho -0.12; run difference +0.003, CI -0.007 to +0.013; post hoc high- vs low-delta clip difference -0.003, CI -0.014 to +0.007). The model with a channel delta covariate again gave about zero (-0.010), because channel delta power measures the knee. FC gradient, S-A axis, thickness and MEG timescale had the predicted sign but failed spin tests (Holm p >= 0.35). All eleven sensitivity variants stayed negative; inferior channels gave a weaker slope (-0.030). Limitations: same patients and electrodes as run-01, so this is a replication across clips and states, not across cohorts; undocumented sleep stage; epilepsy patients; template positions; group maps; spin p only about 0.02; few primary sensory channels.

B: run-02 primary slope against 1,000 spin-null slopes (p_spin 0.022). C: slopes with 95% patient-bootstrap CIs; the model with a channel delta covariate stays near zero.

A: patient-centred log10 tau of 2,380 channels in the two clips (rho 0.85). B: per-patient T1w/T2w slopes in the two clips. C: change in per-patient slope against change in relative delta power between clips (rho -0.12): state does not change the gradient.

A: slopes of six cortical maps without the delta covariate, run-01 (blue, earlier study) and run-02 (orange); only T1w/T2w passes the spin test. B: run-02 sensitivity variants of the T1w/T2w slope (all CIs exclude 0).
